title: Reconciliation
definition: Reconciliation is the restoration of broken relationship through truth, repentance, forgiveness, justice, and grace.
summary: Reconciliation seeks restored relationship where sin has brought separation.
christFocus: Jesus reconciles sinners to God through the cross and creates a people called to pursue peace with one another.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Reconciliation is central to the Gospel. Sin separates people from God, and Christ restores peace through His blood. This vertical reconciliation becomes the foundation for pursuing restored relationships with others.

Biblical reconciliation is not pretending nothing happened. It requires truth, repentance, forgiveness, humility, and sometimes wise boundaries. Reconciliation is deeper than surface peace.

The Church is called to be a reconciled people. Believers should be eager to repair what sin has broken while remembering that full reconciliation requires honest response to truth.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many relationships remain broken because people avoid truth or refuse forgiveness. Reconciliation matters because the Gospel creates a people who pursue peace without denying sin.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: If you have wronged someone, seek reconciliation with humility and repentance. If someone has wronged you, pray for grace, pursue peace where possible, and use wisdom where trust must be rebuilt.
